body:
Kestrel kickoff w/ Meera, Kabir, Zoya. Goal: fix onboarding drop-off - right now only 41% of new users finish signup.
Scope = signup + KYC flow, Android first, iOS later. Zoya owns metrics, Kabir owns feasibility, I own the flows.
Launch target Oct 15.
Me: audit the current flow + competitor teardown by Friday.
Kabir: check if a DigiLocker integration is even possible.

Design of Everyday Things (Norman) - notes ch 1.
Affordance = what an object lets you do. Signifier = the cue that tells you what to do. Most "bad UX" I see at work is
missing signifiers, not missing affordances. Our "Verify" button on the KYC screen looks disabled even when it is
active - classic signifier failure. Also: when users fail, they blame themselves, which is why nobody reports it.

life admin:
- renew bike insurance before 15 July (expires that day!)
- pay credit card bill
- call Hathway AGAIN about slow internet

First week of Kestrel done. Feels good to own a project end to end for once. Haven't run in five days though and I
can feel it. Thinking about signing up for a half marathon in December to force some consistency.

Idea: a weekly review template. Sunday evening, 20 min. Three sections - wins, misses, top 3 for next week.
Could live as a pinned note. Maybe automate the prompt with a reminder.

Competitor teardown (signup + KYC):
- Paywise: 7 steps, manual PAN + Aadhaar photo upload, ~6 min end to end.
- Moneta: 4 steps, video KYC as the main path, long waits in the evenings.
- Kosh: 3 steps, DigiLocker consent pulls documents automatically, ~2 min. Best of the three.
Takeaway: fewer steps + DigiLocker is the pattern to beat.

Registered for the Navi Mumbai half marathon - race day is 13 Dec. Goal: finish under 2:10.
Plan: 20-week build starting Monday 20 July, 4 runs/week (2 easy, 1 tempo, 1 long). Nikhil is doing it too.

Kestrel design review. Decision: go with the 3-step flow, not the 5-step one.
Steps: (1) phone number + OTP, (2) PAN + DigiLocker consent, (3) set app PIN.
Kabir is fine with it if DigiLocker works out. Meera wants a motion prototype of the full flow by 31 July.
Zoya will define the funnel events so we can measure each step.

Thinking in Systems (Meadows), ch 1-2. Stocks and flows: a stock only changes through its inflows and outflows,
so it lags. Our signup funnel is a stock of "half-registered users" - we keep adding inflow (ads) without fixing
the outflow (abandonment). Balancing vs reinforcing loops - word of mouth is a reinforcing loop we're starving.

yaar ek app idea - flatmates ke beech ghar ka kharcha split karne ke liye, but UPI messages se auto-detect ho jaye.
Splitwise jaisa but zero manual entry. Kabhi weekend pe prototype banaunga, abhi time nahi hai.

Tanvi got engaged to Siddharth!! Big family video call tonight, mom was crying happy tears.
Wedding will probably be in February, in Nashik. I already know I'll be roped into the invitations.

Started learning Rust - The Rust Book ch 1-4. Ownership and borrowing are confusing: a value has one owner, you can
have many immutable refs OR one mutable ref, never both. Feels strict but I get why. Goal: build something small
instead of only reading.

Running reference:
easy pace 7:15/km, tempo 6:10/km, long run 7:00-7:20/km.
Race pace for sub-2:10 half = ~6:10/km.
Shoes: daily trainer for easy days, keep the old pair for rain.

1:1 with Meera. Career stuff: she thinks I could be considered for Design Lead in the January review cycle if Kestrel
lands well. I need to start documenting impact, not just shipping. She also wants me to mentor Pooja, the new design
intern. Felt encouraging but also like the bar just moved.

Money decision: switching to the new tax regime this year. ELSS isn't needed for 80C anymore - keep the existing
ELSS units, just stop fresh ELSS investments. Emergency fund is at 1.5 lakh, target is 3 lakh (about 6 months of expenses).

Kestrel sync. Kabir confirmed the DigiLocker API is feasible, so it replaces the manual document upload completely.
Catch: we need certification from the DigiLocker partner team, which usually takes 4-6 weeks.
Kabir to submit the application by 14 Aug. If certification slips, the launch date slips.

buy foam rollr
bday gift for ishita - 20 aug!!
bathroom tap leaking, call plumber sat
return amzn parcel b4 window closes (sun)

Independence Day. Did a 10 km long run at 7:05/km along the Bandra promenade, flags everywhere, really nice
atmosphere. Slept in after. Lazy day with the family on the phone. A good kind of tired.

Finished Deep Work (Newport). Main takeaway: shallow work expands to fill the day unless you schedule depth first.
Going to try two 90-minute deep-work blocks a day, Slack closed, phone in another room. Mornings for design,
afternoons for meetings.

Side project: "streak" - a tiny Rust CLI habit tracker.
Commands: streak add <habit>, streak done <habit>, streak list.
Stack: clap for argument parsing, serde for config, rusqlite for storage (SQLite file in ~/.streak).
Good excuse to actually practise ownership stuff.

Kestrel usability test, round 1, 8 participants.
- 5 of 8 got confused at the "PAN" step label - several didn't know PAN = their tax card. Rename it to "PAN card (tax ID)".
- 2 of 8 couldn't find the "resend OTP" link.
- Everyone liked the DigiLocker auto-fill once they got there.
Me: fix the copy by 28 Aug. Zoya: schedule round 2 for the first week of September.

Idea!! weekly review every Sunday - 20 mins. What went well, what didn't, top 3 priorities for next week.
Could keep it as a template note and duplicate it each week.

Tanvi's wedding date is fixed - 12 February 2027, in Nashik. I'm officially in charge of designing the invitations.
Mom wants our side's guest list by 15 October.

Done with Hathway. Switching to Airtel Xstream fiber - 300 Mbps plan, Rs 999/month. Installation is on 5 Sept.
Cancel Hathway only AFTER the new connection is working.

Guitar: working on the F barre chord. 15 minutes every day before work. Index finger keeps muting the G string.
Watching a few YouTube lessons on thumb position.

Kestrel A/B results are in. New 3-step flow: 58% signup completion vs 41% for the old flow (control).
~12,000 users over two weeks, significant. Biggest remaining drop-off is the DigiLocker consent screen.
This is the number for my impact doc.

Left knee pain on the outer side after today's 14 km run. Had to walk the last km. Booked physio with Dr. Neha Shah
for Tuesday. Skipping running till then.

Physio - Dr. Neha Shah. Diagnosis: IT band syndrome, left knee. Not structural, phew.
Plan: foam roll daily, glute bridges + clamshells 3x15 every day, cap long runs at 12 km for two weeks.
Follow-up appointment 29 Sept.

Finished Thinking in Systems (Meadows). Long note because I want to actually think about this.

The leverage points chapter is the one that stuck. Her list goes roughly from weak to strong: numbers and parameters
(subsidies, taxes, standards) are the least powerful even though they're where everyone spends their energy. Above
that come buffers, stock-and-flow structures, delays, feedback loops, information flows, rules, the power to
self-organise, goals, and at the top, the paradigm the system comes out of.

Applying it to Kestrel: for months the team's answer to drop-off was parameter tweaks - change a button colour,
shorten a label, add a progress bar. Those helped a little. The real jump came from changing the structure: cutting
five steps to three and replacing manual uploads with DigiLocker. That's a stock-and-flow change, not a parameter.
The next level up is information flow - users don't know why we need their PAN, so they hesitate. Telling them
(a short "why we ask" line) might beat any further layout change.

Applying it to running: my knee problem is a delay problem. I increased mileage, the body adapted slowly, and the
damage showed up weeks after the decision that caused it. The fix isn't "run harder", it's respecting the delay -
smaller weekly increases.

Applying it to money: SIPs are a reinforcing loop. The rule "invest first, spend what's left" is a stronger
leverage point than any individual budgeting decision.

Applying it to my career: the goal of the system I'm in rewards shipping, but promotion rewards visible impact.
If I don't change my own information flows - writing down outcomes - the work stays invisible.

Not sure what to do with all of this yet. Mostly I want to remember that the obvious knobs are usually the weak ones.

Rohan called - wants a trip with Ishita and me sometime in November, after Diwali. Options: Lonavala or Mulshi.
Need to decide soonish. Nobody wants to drive more than 3 hours.

Increasing my monthly SIP from 15,000 to 20,000 starting October. Emergency fund is now at 1.8 lakh,
so 1.2 lakh more to hit the 3 lakh target.

Passport expires March 2027 - apply for renewal by end of October, before wedding chaos.
Need: old passport, address proof, book the PSK appointment online.

Kestrel: launch moved from 15 Oct to 5 Nov. Reason: DigiLocker certification is delayed - partner team came back
with extra security questions. Launch will be Android only; iOS follows in December.
Me: update the launch comms deck by 2 Oct. Kabir: answer the security questionnaire this week.

Physio follow-up. Knee is much better. Allowed to rebuild the long run gradually - add max 2 km per week.
Keep the glute work going through race day.

Bit anxious about the Kestrel delay, felt like it reflects on me even though it's a certification thing.
Talked to Nikhil on our run, he said nobody remembers launch dates, they remember whether it worked. Fair.

streak progress: add + list work, data saves to SQLite. Stuck on the borrow checker when returning a Vec<&Habit>
from a function that owns the connection. Probably need to return owned Habits instead.
Goal: publish v0.1 on crates.io by end of November.

Trip decided with Rohan + Ishita: Mulshi, not Lonavala (Lonavala will be packed that weekend).
Dates: 13-15 Nov. Staying at Green Ridge homestay. Budget ~Rs 6,000 per person all-in.
Rohan drives his car. I book the homestay by 10 Oct. Ishita makes the food plan.

Mentoring Pooja - weekly 30-min check-in, Thursdays. She's designing empty states for the transactions screen.
Her instincts are good; she under-explains her decisions. Next session: practise presenting rationale.

Wedding invitation drafts - 3 concepts: marigold (traditional, gold + orange), minimal (cream, serif type),
Warli art (white line figures on terracotta). Tanvi loves the Warli one. Printer needs final files by 30 Nov.
Need Siddharth's family's names spelled correctly in Marathi.
Booked Green Ridge for Mulshi. Paid Rs 4,500 advance, rest on arrival. Shared the booking screenshot in the group.

Rust Book ch 15 - smart pointers. Box<T> for heap allocation, Rc<T> for shared ownership (single thread),
RefCell<T> for interior mutability checked at runtime. Rc<RefCell<T>> = shared + mutable. Might be overkill for streak.

Landlord (Mr. Desai) called. Rent goes up 5% from January; the lease renewal is due 31 Dec.
Asked him about repainting - he'll pay half if I arrange the painter.
Get two painter quotes before the renewal.
Sent mom our side's guest list for the wedding - about 60 people. Done on the deadline, for once.

Kestrel launch readiness. DigiLocker certification approved on 14 Oct!! QA sign-off planned for 30 Oct.
Me: final copy review of all screens by 23 Oct. Zoya: release notes. Kabir: rollout plan at 10% then 100%.

Long run: 16 km at 6:45/km, knee completely fine. Longest run so far. Need to get comfortable at 6:10/km
for the sub-2:10 goal.
Blog post idea: "What 8 usability tests taught me about KYC". Write it after the Kestrel launch, when I can share numbers.

Sangeet ke liye cousins ke saath group dance hai. Song abhi decide nahi hua - Tanvi wants something 90s Bollywood.
Practice weekends pe hi ho payegi. Thoda overwhelming lag raha hai, office + wedding + training sab ek saath.
Song shortlist banana hai is weekend tak.

Mulshi packing list: rain jacket, running shoes (long run on Sat morning), power bank, speaker, cards,
mosquito repellent, cash for the homestay balance.

1:1 with Meera about the Design Lead promotion. I need an impact doc by 15 Dec: Kestrel metrics (41% -> 58%),
mentoring Pooja, my design system contributions. She'll present it in the January review.

Diwali at home in Nashik, 7-9 Nov. Book train tickets by Sunday!! Panchavati Express if available.
Buy gifts for mom, dad and Tanvi.

Week reflection: copy review shipped on time, 16 km long run, guest list done. Didn't touch guitar or streak at all.
I think that's ok for this season. Not everything gets to be a priority at the same time.

Delivered the Kestrel motion prototype. Meera's feedback: transitions feel slow, drop them from 300ms to 200ms,
and the OTP screen should auto-advance once 6 digits are in.

Kestrel copy guidelines (for me + Pooja):
plain language, no jargon without explanation, aim for an 8th-grade reading level, always say why we're asking
for a document, error messages say what to do next.

Kestrel v2 ideas: video KYC as a fallback when DigiLocker fails; auto-fill PAN from DigiLocker instead of asking;
a "why we ask" tooltip on every document step.

Mom's poha tips from the phone call: rinse the poha, don't soak; add a pinch of sugar with the salt;
peanuts fried first, curry leaves last; squeeze lime only after taking it off the flame.
streak todo: write README, add unit tests for the add/done commands, set up GitHub Actions CI.

Annual checkup results: everything normal except Vitamin D, which is low at 14 ng/mL.
Doctor prescribed 60,000 IU once a week for 8 weeks. Recheck blood test in November.

Guitar: the F barre chord finally rings clean! Next: learn two strumming patterns properly and play one full song
start to finish.

Kestrel metrics sync with Zoya. Funnel events: signup_started, otp_verified, pan_submitted, digilocker_consented,
pin_set. Baseline completion 41%. Target for launch: 55%.

Should catch up with Kabir sometime next week about the post-launch analytics dashboard.
Also need to think about Q1 OKRs at some point.
